On that last point --- I prefer incorporating the assignment of rents into the mortgage body rather than executing it as a separate instrument for this deal. That approach reduces recording costs and streamlines enforcement. See my detailed notes below in Section 3.

Define **\"Property\"** broadly to include all three tax parcels (460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009) and the vacated Anson Lane strip. Define **\"Loan Documents\"** to cross-reference the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC (SC License No. SC-GC-47921), the renovation budget, and all reserve agreements. Define **\"Guarantor\"** as Neil Ashford Graydon, individually, of 14 Church Street, Charleston, SC 29401. Define **\"Maturity Date\"** as April 15, 2030.

**[2. Granting Clause and Legal Description]{.underline}**

Use the legal description from the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective date February 28, 2025, underwritten by Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc.): Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, together with the former Anson Lane strip vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the aforesaid RMC Office.

**CRITICAL --- ANSON LANE CHAIN OF TITLE.** Jordan --- the Anson Lane strip was conveyed to the borrower\'s predecessor by quitclaim deed only (Deed Book 1128, Page 443). A quitclaim deed provides no warranties of title whatsoever. We need to verify three things before we can be comfortable with this parcel as mortgaged collateral: (1) that the title commitment from Prestige Title and Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. affirmatively insures fee simple title to the Anson Lane strip without any Schedule B-II exception that carves it out or qualifies the estate as less than fee simple; (2) that the vesting chain from the City of Charleston through the quitclaim deed to the current seller and then to borrower is complete and unbroken, with no gaps in ownership or intervening claims; and (3) whether we should request a specific title endorsement --- an ALTA 9 endorsement or equivalent --- covering this parcel separately to ensure the lender has specific affirmative insurance against loss arising from a title defect in the strip. Review the title commitment Schedule B-II carefully. If the Anson Lane strip is excepted, shown as less than fee simple, or qualified in any way, we have a gap in collateral coverage. This is a non-trivial issue because the strip connects Lots 7 through 9 and its loss could impair vehicular and pedestrian access to the Property and undermine the approved site plan. Flag this for Prestige Title immediately and copy me on any correspondence.

The granting clause should convey a mortgage lien on fee simple title to the Property, together with all improvements now or hereafter erected thereon, all fixtures, building systems, equipment, and appurtenances. Include the standard \"together with\" language for rents, profits, issues, and all other collateral described in the mortgage. Reference all three tax map numbers in the granting clause itself, in addition to the full metes and bounds description in Exhibit A.

Note: The legal description should be set out in **Exhibit A** to the mortgage and referenced in the granting clause by incorporation. We will need the surveyor\'s legal description (metes and bounds) in addition to the plat reference --- confirm with the borrower\'s surveyor that the ALTA/NSPS survey has been ordered and will be delivered in certified form before the closing date.

**[3. Assignment of Leases, Rents, and Profits]{.underline}**

**IMPORTANT --- ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT REQUIRED.** Our template currently uses a collateral assignment of rents, which is the older approach and is insufficient for this deal. South Carolina enacted the Uniform Assignment of Rents Act (S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*), and we need to draft this provision as an **absolute assignment** of all leases, rents, issues, and profits of the Property, not merely a collateral assignment. Under the SC statute, an absolute assignment is effective upon execution and recording; the lender\'s right to collect rents is perfected upon recording in the county land records but enforcement --- meaning actual collection of rents by the lender --- is triggered only by borrower default. Revise the template language throughout to remove any \"collateral\" or \"as additional security\" characterization and replace it with \"absolute and present\" assignment language. The operative provision should state affirmatively that borrower unconditionally and absolutely transfers and assigns to Lender all right, title, and interest in and to all current and future leases, subleases, and occupancy agreements affecting the Property, and all rents, income, revenues, issues, profits, and other sums now or hereafter payable thereunder, without reservation.

**CRITICAL --- LOWCOUNTRY PROVISIONS LEASE --- NO ASSIGNMENT/CONSENT CLAUSE.** I\'ve reviewed the lease abstracts from the rent roll in detail. The Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease (Bay 1, approximately 3,800 SF, \$28.50/SF NNN, lease expiration December 31, 2027) has no assignment or subletting provision whatsoever --- the lease abstract notes \"Assignment/Subletting: No provision.\" This is unusual for a commercial lease and creates a significant wrinkle. Under S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*, the assignment of rents is enforceable against a tenant upon notification regardless of what the underlying lease says about assignment, so we are legally covered from a pure enforceability standpoint. However, a tenant whose lease contains no express consent-to-assignment clause could raise practical objections or withhold cooperation at the very moment we need to enforce --- and the last thing the bank wants in a workout is a tenant claiming it didn\'t consent to paying rent to the lender.

Best practice here requires three steps: **(a)** require borrower to represent and warrant in the mortgage that it has the full right and authority to assign all rents under all leases affecting the Property, including specifically and without limitation the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease; **(b)** require delivery of a **tenant estoppel certificate** from Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a condition precedent to closing, in which the tenant acknowledges the existence of the mortgage, the assignment of rents to the lender, and agrees to pay rent to the lender upon written notice following a borrower default; and **(c)** include a post-closing covenant requiring borrower to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a lease amendment to the Lowcountry Provisions lease adding a standard assignment-consent provision at the next renewal, extension, or amendment opportunity. Flag this item for Marcus at the bank --- he should know that the Lowcountry Provisions estoppel is critical and should not be waived.

The other two occupied leases are lower-risk on this point but still require estoppels at closing:

> • **Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC** (Bay 3, approximately 3,800 SF, \$24.00/SF modified gross, lease expiration June 30, 2026) --- the lease abstract shows a standard landlord assignment consent clause. Estoppel required at closing but lower risk.
>
> • **Tidemark Consulting Group LLC** (2nd Floor Suite A, approximately 9,800 SF, \$22.00/SF NNN, lease expiration March 31, 2029) --- same, standard consent-to-assignment provision in the lease. Estoppel required at closing.

The mortgage should grant borrower a revocable license to collect rents until the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default. Upon default, lender may collect rents directly upon written notice to tenants without the necessity of obtaining a court order or appointing a receiver, though we should also include the standard provisions for lender\'s right to seek appointment of a receiver in any judicial proceeding to enforce the mortgage.

**[4. Single-Purpose Entity Covenants]{.underline}**

**CRITICAL --- SPE COVENANTS VS. OPERATING AGREEMENT.** The term sheet requires full single-purpose entity covenants for Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC. I\'ve reviewed the redacted summary of the borrower\'s operating agreement provided by borrower\'s counsel, and it does **not** currently contain any of the following provisions, all of which we will need:

**(1) Independent Director/Manager Requirement.** The operating agreement designates Graydon Development Group LLC as the sole managing member with exclusive management authority. There is no provision whatsoever for an independent director or independent manager whose affirmative consent is required before the borrower may file a voluntary bankruptcy petition, consent to an involuntary bankruptcy petition, dissolve, merge, consolidate, or wind up its affairs. We need this provision for bankruptcy remoteness --- without it, Graydon Development Group LLC could unilaterally file the borrower into bankruptcy, which defeats the entire purpose of the SPE structure.

**(2) Separateness Covenants.** The operating agreement does not include standard separateness covenants. We need the borrower to covenant that it shall at all times: maintain separate books and records; maintain separate bank accounts; not commingle its assets with those of any affiliate; hold itself out to the public as a separate legal entity; use its own stationery, invoices, and checks; not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any affiliate; pay its own liabilities from its own assets; maintain arm\'s-length relationships with affiliates; and maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business.

**(3) Restriction to Single Purpose.** The operating agreement\'s purpose clause appears to allow \"any lawful business\" --- a standard boilerplate formulation. We need this narrowed to a single-purpose restriction: the borrower\'s sole purpose is owning, operating, managing, leasing, and financing the Property at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403, and activities incidental thereto.

**(4) Member Consent.** Here is the complication. The borrower has three members with potentially divergent economic and governance interests: **Graydon Development Group LLC** (72% membership interest), **Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP** (18% membership interest), and **Harborline Capital Advisors LLC** (10% membership interest). The SPE covenants --- especially the independent director requirement and the restriction on voluntary bankruptcy filings --- must be binding on all members, not just the managing member. We need written confirmation that Tidewater and Harborline have reviewed the SPE restrictions, understand their implications, and have consented to be bound by them. The operating agreement summary I reviewed does not reflect any such consent.

**ACTION ITEMS:**

> \(a\) Draft the SPE covenants in the mortgage as though the operating agreement already contains compliant provisions --- that is, include representations and warranties that the borrower\'s organizational documents contain SPE provisions satisfying the lender\'s requirements.
>
> \(b\) Separately, prepare a form of **Operating Agreement Amendment** adding the independent director requirement, separateness covenants, single-purpose restriction, and unanimity requirement for bankruptcy filings, dissolution, and merger.
>
> \(c\) Make delivery of the executed Operating Agreement Amendment --- signed by **all three members** (Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC) --- a **condition precedent to closing**.
>
> \(d\) Include a covenant in the mortgage that borrower shall not amend, modify, or waive any SPE provision of its operating agreement without the lender\'s prior written consent in each instance.

One additional note: **Tidewater GP Holdings LLC** is the general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP. Confirm that Tidewater GP Holdings LLC has the authority to bind the fund to the operating agreement amendment. Check the limited partnership agreement or, if that is not available, request a GP authorization certificate or resolution prior to closing.

**[5. Prepayment / Yield Maintenance]{.underline}**

The prepayment structure from the term sheet is as follows: a 24-month absolute lockout period (months 1--24), followed by yield maintenance (months 25--48), followed by open prepayment with no premium (months 49--60, i.e., the final 12 months before the April 15, 2030 Maturity Date).

**CRITICAL --- YIELD MAINTENANCE FORMULA MUST BE PRECISE.** The term sheet describes the prepayment premium as \"yield maintenance (treasury rate + 50 bps spread)\" but does not specify several critical variables, each of which must be defined with precision in the mortgage:

> **(a)** Which U.S. Treasury rate? The Constant Maturity Treasury (CMT) rate? If so, for what tenor --- matched to the remaining term of the loan from the prepayment date to maturity? Matched to the remaining yield maintenance period? Interpolated between two published tenors if no exact match exists?
>
> **(b)** How is the present value of remaining payments calculated? Is the discount rate the Treasury rate alone, or the Treasury rate plus the 50 basis point spread referenced in the term sheet?
>
> **(c)** Is the prepayment premium the greater of the yield maintenance amount or some fixed minimum percentage of the prepaid principal (e.g., 1%), or is it the yield maintenance amount standing alone with no minimum?
>
> **(d)** What happens if the calculated yield maintenance premium is zero or negative --- that is, if Treasury rates have risen sufficiently since origination that there is no present-value differential? Is there a floor of zero, or is there a minimum premium regardless?

**South Carolina enforceability concern.** SC courts have generally enforced yield maintenance premiums in commercial loan transactions as reasonable liquidated damages provisions, but the formula must be specific, mathematically deterministic, and objectively calculable at the time of prepayment. If the formula is ambiguous or requires subjective judgment calls, a court could deem it an unenforceable penalty or refuse to enforce it on grounds of indefiniteness. We dealt with precisely this issue in a prior transaction approximately two years ago, and I do not want a repeat.

**DRAFTING INSTRUCTION.** Insert a precise, self-contained yield maintenance formula in the mortgage substantially as follows:

> *\"The Yield Maintenance Premium shall equal the positive excess, if any, of (A) the present value of all remaining scheduled monthly payments of interest and principal from the prepayment date through the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period (the payment due on or about month 48 following the date of the Note), discounted monthly at a per annum rate equal to the Treasury Rate, over (B) the outstanding principal amount being prepaid. The \"Treasury Rate\" shall mean the yield to maturity, as of the second Business Day preceding the prepayment date, of the United States Treasury security (as reported in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 --- Selected Interest Rates, or any successor publication) having a maturity date closest to, but not exceeding, the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period. If no published maturity exactly matches, interpolate linearly between the two nearest published maturities. In no event shall the Yield Maintenance Premium be less than zero.\"*

A key interpretive question: the 50 basis points referenced in the term sheet. Add the 50 bps to the **loan rate** (not to the Treasury rate) when computing the stream of remaining payments to be discounted --- that is, the remaining payments should be calculated at the Note rate, and the spread over Treasuries reflects the lender\'s bargained-for return. Confirm this interpretation with Marcus before finalizing. The term sheet\'s reference to \"treasury rate + 50 bps spread\" is ambiguous on its face and could reasonably be read either way.

Include the lockout provision as an **absolute prohibition** on voluntary prepayment during months 1 through 24, with no exception other than the application of casualty insurance proceeds or condemnation awards, which should be applied at par without any prepayment premium. Confirm this casualty/condemnation carve-out with the client --- some lenders want a premium even on involuntary prepayments, though that is the minority position.

The following sections of the template require customization but are more straightforward. Brief notes on each:

**Security Interest / UCC Collateral. Standard Article 9 language. Ensure we cover all personal property, fixtures (file as a fixture filing in the Charleston County RMC and as a UCC-1 financing statement with the SC Secretary of State), equipment, accounts, general intangibles, insurance proceeds, condemnation proceeds, permits, licenses, contracts (including the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC), and all reserve accounts held by the lender. The UCC-1 should name Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC (EIN: 84-6213750) as debtor and Calverley Heritage Bank as secured party. Confirm the collateral description in the UCC-1 matches the mortgage.**

**Renovation Disbursement Provisions.** The holdback is \$2,250,000 against a total renovation budget of \$3,150,000 --- the term sheet contemplates periodic draws from the holdback upon satisfaction of disbursement conditions. Build in standard draw procedures: written draw request with not less than ten business days\' advance notice, architect\'s certification of percentage completion, unconditional lien waivers from Beaufort Builders Group LLC and all subcontractors for all work covered by prior draws, a title endorsement (no intervening liens since last draw), and 10% retainage until substantial completion. Substantial completion deadline is June 15, 2026. Cross-reference the completion guaranty from Neil Ashford Graydon, which guarantees the borrower\'s obligation to complete the renovation on budget and on schedule.

**Insurance Covenants.** Standard commercial property coverage: all-risk (special form) at full replacement cost, commercial general liability (\$2,000,000 per occurrence / \$5,000,000 aggregate), builder\'s risk during the renovation period, and the reserve/escrow provisions for insurance premiums. The template should be fine here --- just update the coverage amounts and add the builder\'s risk requirement for the construction phase.

**Financial Covenants.** DSCR minimum of 1.25x, tested quarterly on a trailing twelve-month basis, beginning 24 months post-closing (first test date April 15, 2027). Guarantor minimum net worth of not less than \$1,000,000, tested annually. Guarantor minimum liquid assets of not less than \$500,000, tested annually. Audited financial statements of borrower within 120 days of fiscal year end. Quarterly rent rolls within 30 days of each calendar quarter end. These are all specified in the term sheet --- populate the template accordingly.

**Default and Remedies.** Standard default provisions. Ensure we include SC-specific foreclosure language --- South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state with no power of sale. The mortgage should not purport to grant a power of sale. Cross-default to the Note, the Guaranty Agreement, and the Environmental Indemnity Agreement. Default rate of interest: the applicable rate plus 5.00% per annum. Late charge: 5% of any installment of principal or interest not received within 10 calendar days of its due date.

**Governing Law / Recording.** South Carolina law governs. The mortgage will be recorded in the Charleston County Register of Mesne Conveyance. Confirm documentary stamp tax and recording fee calculations with Prestige Title before closing. The mortgage tax in South Carolina is 0.37% of the indebtedness secured --- on \$14,750,000, that is \$54,575.00. Budget accordingly.

**Environmental Covenants.** Use our standard template environmental compliance covenant. The Phase I ESA from Clearfield Environmental Consulting came back clean except for the controlled recognized environmental condition, which has a no-further-action letter on file. The Environmental Indemnity Agreement is a separate document executed by borrower and guarantor and will handle the substantive environmental risk allocation. Standard provisions in the mortgage should suffice.

**[Closing Notes]{.underline}**

Jordan --- let me know if you have questions on any of the foregoing. Prioritize the assignment of rents restructuring (switching from collateral to absolute assignment), the SPE/operating agreement issue (including the form of operating agreement amendment), and the yield maintenance formula. Those are the three most complex drafting tasks and I want to see them handled correctly in the first draft. I want to see a clean initial draft by **March 28** so we have time for internal review before sending to Marcus on April 1.

Also, do not forget to confirm the Anson Lane chain of title with Prestige Title early in the process --- if there is a gap in the title to that strip, we need to know well before we get deep into document drafting and negotiate ourselves into a corner.

One more thought --- coordinate with Marcus on whether the bank\'s loan committee or board has approved any exceptions to standard underwriting guidelines for this loan. The as-is LTV runs a little hot. He\'ll know what I mean.

Kit

No Member may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, encumber, or otherwise dispose of (collectively, \"**Transfer**\") all or any portion of its Membership Interest in the Company without the prior written consent of the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Membership Interests, calculated by excluding the Transferring Member\'s own interest from the denominator used in determining the 75% threshold. Any Transfer made in violation of this Section 4 shall be void and of no force or effect, and the Company and the remaining Members shall not be obligated to recognize or give effect to any such attempted Transfer. The transfer restrictions in this Section 4 apply exclusively to Transfers of Membership Interests in the Company and do not purport to restrict or address changes in the internal or upstream ownership, management, or control of any Member entity.

**4.2 Permitted Transfers**

Notwithstanding the general restriction set forth in Section 4.1, the following Transfers are designated as \"**Permitted Transfers**\" and do not require the consent of the Managing Member or any other Member:

> \(a\) Transfers by any Member to an Affiliate of such Member, as defined in Section 4.5, provided that the transferee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of the Operating Agreement;
>
> \(b\) Transfers by GDG to any trust established by Neil Ashford Graydon for estate planning purposes, provided that Neil Ashford Graydon retains voting and management control over the transferred Membership Interest during his lifetime;
>
> \(c\) Transfers by Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP directed by its general partner, Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, including transfers to any successor fund managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate thereof, without the consent of any other Member;
>
> \(d\) Transfers among existing Members.

Section 4.2(c) is particularly broad in scope. It grants Tidewater GP Holdings LLC the sole authority to direct Transfers of Tidewater\'s 18% Membership Interest, not only to Affiliates of Tidewater but also to any \"successor fund\" managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC. The term \"successor fund\" is not defined in the Operating Agreement. This provision could result in the Transfer of Tidewater\'s 18% Membership Interest to a fund entity that is under substantially different economic beneficial ownership than Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, so long as Tidewater GP Holdings LLC (or an Affiliate thereof) serves as the manager or general partner of such successor fund. No consent from GDG, Harborline, or any third party is required for such a Transfer.

The Operating Agreement does not contain any provision restricting or requiring consent for changes in the internal ownership, control, or management of any Member at the entity level. By way of illustration:

> • Neil Ashford Graydon could sell or transfer his membership interest in GDG, the 72% Managing Member, to a third party. Because the Membership Interest in the Company would continue to be held in the name of GDG, no Transfer of a Membership Interest in the Company would occur, and the restrictions in Section 4.1 would not be triggered.
>
> • Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, the general partner of Tidewater, could itself be acquired by, merged with, or replaced by a new entity. Such a change would effectively alter who controls the 18% Membership Interest held by Tidewater, but would not constitute a Transfer of a Membership Interest in the Company.
>
> • The internal membership or management of Harborline Capital Advisors LLC could change entirely without triggering the Transfer restrictions, because the Membership Interest in the Company would remain registered in the name of Harborline.

The Operating Agreement contains no \"change of control\" provision that would capture indirect or upstream transfers or that would require notice to, or consent from, the Company or its Members in connection with any such change.

**4.3 Right of First Offer**

If any Member desires to Transfer all or any portion of its Membership Interest other than pursuant to a Permitted Transfer, such Member (the \"**Offering Member**\") must first deliver to the Company and the remaining Members a written offer (the \"**Transfer Notice**\") setting forth the proposed price, terms, and conditions of the proposed Transfer and the identity of the proposed third-party transferee. The remaining Members shall have the right, exercisable within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Transfer Notice, to elect to purchase the offered Membership Interest pro rata in proportion to their respective Membership Interests (excluding the Offering Member\'s interest) at the same price and on the same terms set forth in the Transfer Notice. If the remaining Members decline or fail to exercise their right of first offer within such thirty (30) day period, the Offering Member may consummate the proposed Transfer to the proposed third-party transferee within ninety (90) days of the expiration of the right of first offer period, provided that such Transfer is on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice.

**4.4 Tag-Along and Drag-Along Rights**

\[Redacted --- Tag-along and drag-along provisions summarized as follows: If GDG proposes to Transfer 50% or more of its Membership Interest to a third party, the Passive Members have tag-along rights permitting them to participate in such Transfer on the same price and terms. If Members holding 80% or more of the outstanding Membership Interests approve a sale of the Company or the Property to a third party, they may require all other Members to participate in such sale on the same terms and conditions (drag-along). Detailed mechanics redacted.\]

**4.5 Definition of \"Affiliate\"**

The Operating Agreement defines \"**Affiliate**\" as follows:

> \"with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with, such Person. \'Control\' means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.\"

This is a standard \"control\"-based Affiliate definition. However, the Permitted Transfer provision in Section 4.2(c) extends beyond transfers to Affiliates of Tidewater --- it permits transfers to \"any successor fund managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate thereof.\" A successor fund managed by an Affiliate of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC could be under substantially different ultimate economic ownership than Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP itself, yet such a transfer would qualify as a Permitted Transfer not requiring any consent. The interaction of the Affiliate definition with the Permitted Transfer carve-outs creates a broad pathway for the transfer of Tidewater\'s 18% interest outside the ordinary consent requirements.

**[Section 5: Distributions]{.underline}**

**5.1 Distribution Waterfall**

Distributable Cash Flow, defined as net cash flow from operations after payment of operating expenses, debt service, and required reserves (but before capital expenditures funded from reserves), shall be distributed to the Members in the following order of priority:

> **First**, to all Members, pro rata in accordance with their respective Membership Interests, until each Member has received cumulative distributions under this tier equal to an eight percent (8%) per annum preferred return on such Member\'s unreturned capital contributions (the \"**Preferred Return**\"). The Preferred Return shall accrue and compound annually to the extent not distributed in any given period.
>
> **Second**, to all Members, pro rata in accordance with their respective Membership Interests, until each Member has received cumulative distributions under this tier and all prior tiers equal to one hundred percent (100%) of such Member\'s aggregate capital contributions.
>
> **Third**, thereafter, eighty percent (80%) to GDG and twenty percent (20%) to the Passive Members. The Passive Members\' share of the Third tier shall be allocated among the Passive Members pro rata based on their respective Passive Member Membership Interests (i.e., Tidewater receives 20% × 18/28 ≈ 12.86% and Harborline receives 20% × 10/28 ≈ 7.14%) (the \"**Promote**\").

The Third tier reflect a promote or carried interest structure for GDG, the Managing Member, which is typical in real estate joint venture arrangements.

**5.2 Distributions from Capital Events**

\[Redacted --- Capital event distribution provisions (including distributions from sale, refinancing, condemnation, or casualty proceeds) summarized as follows: Capital event proceeds are distributed in the same waterfall priority as Section 5.1, except that the Third tier promote split is seventy/thirty (70% to GDG and 30% to Passive Members) for capital events. Detailed capital event distribution mechanics, including clawback provisions, are redacted.\]

**5.3 Tax Distributions**

\[Redacted --- The Operating Agreement provides that the Company shall make quarterly tax distributions to the Members in amounts estimated to be sufficient to cover each Member\'s federal and state tax liabilities arising from allocations of Company taxable income for such quarter. Tax distributions are treated as advances against distributions otherwise payable under Section 5.1 and shall reduce amounts otherwise distributable to each recipient Member. Detailed provisions redacted.\]

**[Section 6: Accounting and Reports]{.underline}**

**6.1 Books and Records**

The Managing Member shall maintain, or cause to be maintained, complete and accurate books and records of the Company at the Company\'s principal office located at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401. Each Member and its duly authorized representatives shall have the right to inspect and copy such books and records during normal business hours upon reasonable prior written notice to the Managing Member. The books and records of the Company shall be maintained on the accrual basis of accounting in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied.

**6.2 Financial Reporting**

The Managing Member shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Member the following financial reports:

> \(a\) **Quarterly Financial Statements**: Unaudited quarterly financial statements of the Company, including a balance sheet and statement of income and cash flows, within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter;
>
> \(b\) **Annual Financial Statements**: Annual financial statements of the Company, reviewed (but not audited) by an independent certified public accountant selected by the Managing Member, within ninety (90) days after the end of each fiscal year; and
>
> \(c\) **Schedule K-1s**: IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) for each Member, within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year.

The Operating Agreement requires only \"reviewed\" financial statements on an annual basis --- not audited financial statements. This standard of financial reporting is lower than the audited financial statement requirement that may be imposed by the proposed loan documents.

**6.3 Fiscal Year**

The fiscal year of the Company is the calendar year, commencing January 1 and ending December 31 of each year.

**[Section 7: Exculpation and Indemnification]{.underline}**

\[Redacted --- Exculpation and indemnification provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: The Operating Agreement contains standard provisions exculpating the Managing Member and its Affiliates from liability to the Company or any Member for any act or omission taken in good faith, except for liability arising from fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence. The Operating Agreement further provides for indemnification of the Managing Member and its Affiliates by the Company from Company assets for claims arising out of or relating to the Managing Member\'s service in such capacity, subject to the same carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, and gross negligence.\]

**[Section 8: Dissolution and Winding Up]{.underline}**

**8.1 Events of Dissolution**

The Company shall be dissolved upon the earliest to occur of the following events:

> \(a\) The sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of the Property and the distribution of all net proceeds therefrom to the Members in accordance with Section 5;
>
> \(b\) The prior written consent of Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding Membership Interests;
>
> \(c\) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under S.C. Code Ann. § 33-44-701; or
>
> \(d\) The occurrence of any event that makes it unlawful for the Company to continue its business.

The Operating Agreement does not include any provision requiring the consent of any lender, independent director, independent manager, or other third party as a condition to the voluntary dissolution of the Company. There is no separateness covenant within the dissolution provisions or elsewhere in the Operating Agreement providing that the Company shall not dissolve, liquidate, or wind up its affairs without the prior written consent of the Company\'s secured lender. As noted above, the 75% approval threshold for dissolution under Section 8.1(b) requires GDG\'s participation but does not require unanimous consent of all Members or consent of an independent party.

**8.2 Winding Up**

\[Redacted --- Winding up provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: Upon dissolution, the Managing Member (or a liquidating trustee appointed by Members holding a majority of the Membership Interests, if GDG is unable or unwilling to serve) shall wind up the Company\'s affairs, liquidate its assets in an orderly manner, discharge or make provision for the Company\'s liabilities to creditors, and distribute remaining assets to the Members in accordance with their positive capital account balances.\]

**[Section 9: Miscellaneous Provisions]{.underline}**

**9.1 Amendments.** The Operating Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding Membership Interests; *provided, however*, that no amendment that would (i) alter the economic rights of any Member, including but not limited to such Member\'s rights under the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 5, or (ii) increase any Member\'s capital contribution obligation beyond amounts previously committed, shall be effective without the prior written consent of each Member so affected. The Operating Agreement does not contain any provision requiring the consent of any lender or other third-party creditor as a condition to amendments.

**9.2 Governing Law**

The Operating Agreement is governed by and shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina, without regard to the conflicts of laws principles thereof.

**9.3 Notices.** All notices, demands, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under the Operating Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered by hand, sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service, or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed to the relevant Member at the address set forth in Section 2.1 or at such other address as such Member may designate by written notice to the Company and the other Members. Email notice is permitted for routine business communications but shall not be effective for notices of default, capital calls, or any Major Decision requiring Member approval.

**9.4 Entire Agreement**

The Operating Agreement, together with all exhibits and schedules thereto, constitutes the entire agreement among the Members with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether written or oral, among the Members relating to the Company.

**9.5 Severability.** If any provision of the Operating Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of the Operating Agreement, and the Operating Agreement shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been contained therein.

**9.6 Dispute Resolution**

\[Redacted --- Dispute resolution provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: The Operating Agreement contains a mandatory mediation provision, requiring the Members to submit any dispute arising under the Operating Agreement to mediation in Charleston, South Carolina, prior to initiating any other form of dispute resolution. If mediation is unsuccessful, the dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration in Charleston, South Carolina, administered under the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. Detailed procedural provisions redacted.\]

**[Section 10: Signature Page Summary]{.underline}**

The Amended and Restated Operating Agreement was originally executed as of January 12, 2024, by the following parties:

The amendment dated March 1, 2025, was executed by all three Members listed above. The specific terms and modifications effected by such amendment have not been summarized in this document. Borrower\'s counsel will make the amendment available for review upon request.

**[Appendix: Redaction Notice and Disclaimer]{.underline}**

This Redacted Summary has been prepared by Cartwright & Lyons LLP, counsel to Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC (the \"Borrower\"), for the limited purpose of facilitating the review of the Borrower\'s organizational structure by Calverley Heritage Bank (the \"Lender\") and its counsel, Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP, in connection with the proposed \$14,750,000 commercial mortgage loan from the Lender to the Borrower.

This summary is not a substitute for review of the complete Amended and Restated Operating Agreement. Redacted provisions include, without limitation: (i) detailed capital account maintenance and adjustment provisions; (ii) tax allocation provisions, including provisions relating to allocations under Sections 704(b) and 704(c) of the Internal Revenue Code; (iii) indemnification provisions, including procedures for claims and advancement of expenses; (iv) detailed distribution mechanics for capital events, including clawback and true-up provisions; (v) dispute resolution procedures, including mediation and arbitration mechanics; (vi) tag-along and drag-along mechanics, including timing, notice, and pricing provisions; and (vii) all exhibits and schedules to the Operating Agreement, including Member contribution schedules, forms of assignment and assumption, and forms of joinder agreement.

Calverley Heritage Bank and its counsel are advised to request the full unredacted Operating Agreement, including all exhibits and schedules thereto, for purposes of confirming compliance with any single-purpose entity requirements, separateness covenants, bankruptcy remoteness provisions, or other organizational requirements imposed by the loan documents. Compliance with such requirements cannot be confirmed on the basis of this Redacted Summary alone.

"""Generate a .docx from markdown via Pandoc with an optional reference template.

Usage:
    python generate_from_md.py input.md output.docx [template.docx]

Pandoc applies the template's paragraph and run styles to your markdown.
Best for reports/memos/letters where the template carries firm styling.

Requires pandoc on PATH.
"""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def generate(md_path: Path, output_path: Path, template_path: Path | None = None):
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cmd = ["pandoc", str(md_path), "-o", str(output_path)]
    if template_path is not None:
        cmd.append(f"--reference-doc={template_path}")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"pandoc failed: {result.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        print("Usage: generate_from_md.py <input.md> <output.docx> [template.docx]", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    template = Path(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) == 4 else None
    generate(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), template)

FONT = 'Times New Roman'

    f = style.font
    f.name = FONT

# ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

**1.1 Defined Terms.** As used in this Mortgage and Security Agreement (this "**Mortgage**"), the following terms have the meanings set forth below. Terms used in this Mortgage that are defined in Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of South Carolina (the "**UCC**") and that are not otherwise defined in this Mortgage have the meanings given to them in the UCC.

"**Affiliate**" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with, such Person. "**Control**" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through the ownership of voting interests, by contract, or otherwise.

"**Applicable Rate**" means, for any day, a rate per annum equal to the sum of (a) Daily SOFR for such day (but in no event less than the SOFR Floor), plus (b) two hundred eighty-five basis points (2.85%). Because the SOFR Floor is three percent (3.00%) per annum, the Applicable Rate shall in no event be less than five and 85/100 percent (5.85%) per annum.

"**Approved Renovation Budget**" means the renovation budget for the Project in the aggregate amount of $3,150,000, allocated among line items as set forth in **Exhibit C**, as the same may be revised from time to time only with Mortgagee's prior written consent.

"**Assignment of Rents**" means the absolute and present assignment of Leases, Rents, issues and profits contained in **Article 5** of this Mortgage.

"**Borrower Equity Contribution**" means the sum of $900,000 that Mortgagor is required to contribute from its own funds (and not from the proceeds of the Loan) toward the Renovation Costs, being 28.57% of the Approved Renovation Budget, in accordance with the Draw Schedule attached as part of **Exhibit C**.

"**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in Savannah, Georgia or Charleston, South Carolina are authorized or required by law to be closed.

"**Capital Replacement Reserve**" means the reserve account established and maintained with Mortgagee under Section 8.2.

"**Collateral**" means the Property and all other property, real, personal and mixed, tangible and intangible, now owned or hereafter acquired by Mortgagor in which a Lien is granted to Mortgagee under this Mortgage, including, without limitation, all property described in **Article 3** and **Article 4**.

"**Completion Guaranty**" means the completion guaranty described in Section 4.6 of the Term Sheet, to be executed and delivered by Guarantor in favor of Mortgagee.

"**Condemnation**" means any taking of all or any part of the Property, or of any interest therein or right accruing thereto, by any Governmental Authority, whether by exercise of the power of eminent domain, condemnation, purchase in lieu thereof, or otherwise, and any change of grade or access affecting the Property.

"**Daily SOFR**" means, for any day, the Secured Overnight Financing Rate as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or a successor administrator) on such Business Day, or, if such rate is not published on such Business Day, the rate published on the immediately preceding Business Day; *provided* that if Daily SOFR is not available for any reason, the rate shall be determined in accordance with **Section 15.11**.

"**Default Rate**" means a rate per annum equal to the Applicable Rate plus five percent (5.00%) per annum, as provided in **Section 15.3**.

"**Draw**" and "**Draw Request**" have the meanings given in **Section 10.3**.

"**Environmental Indemnity Agreement**" means the Environmental Indemnity Agreement of even date herewith executed by Mortgagor and Guarantor in favor of Mortgagee, as the same may be amended, restated, supplemented or replaced from time to time.

"**Environmental Law**" means any federal, state or local statute, regulation, ordinance, order, judgment, permit or common law rule relating to pollution, the protection of human health or the environment, or the use, generation, storage, treatment, transportation, disposal, release or threatened release of Hazardous Materials, including, without limitation, the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 9601 *et seq.*, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 6901 *et seq.*, the Clean Water Act, 33 U.S.C. §§ 1251 *et seq.*, the Clean Air Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 7401 *et seq.*, the Toxic Substances Control Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 2601 *et seq.*, and the South Carolina Hazardous Waste Management Act and the South Carolina Pollution Control Act, in each case as amended.

"**Event of Default**" has the meaning given in **Article 12**.

"**Escrow Funds**" means all funds, and all interest and earnings thereon, held by Mortgagee under **Article 9**, the Renovation Holdback, and all other reserves, escrows, deposits and impounds required under any Loan Document.

"**GAAP**" means generally accepted accounting principles in the United States, consistently applied.

"**GC Contract**" means the executed construction contract between Mortgagor, as owner, and Beaufort Builders Group LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company (South Carolina General Contractor License No. SC-GC-47921), as general contractor, in the contract sum of $2,850,000, together with all schedules, exhibits, amendments, change orders and modifications thereto approved by Mortgagee.

"**Governmental Authority**" means the United States, the State of South Carolina, the City of Charleston, Charleston County, and any other federal, state, regional, county, municipal or local government, or any department, agency, commission, board, bureau, court or instrumentality thereof, including, without limitation, SCDHEC, the Charleston County Register of Mesne Conveyances ("**RMC Office**"), and the City of Charleston Board of Architectural Review.

"**Guarantor**" means Neil Ashford Graydon, an individual residing at 14 Church Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29401, and his successors and permitted assigns.

"**Guaranty Agreement**" means the Guaranty Agreement of even date herewith executed by Guarantor in favor of Mortgagee, together with the Completion Guaranty and the interest-shortfall payment guaranty described in Section 5.5(c) of the Term Sheet, as the same may be amended, restated, supplemented or replaced from time to time.

"**Hazardous Materials**" means petroleum and petroleum products, perchloroethylene and other chlorinated solvents, volatile organic compounds, asbestos, polychlorinated biphenyls, radioactive materials, urea formaldehyde, lead-based paint, mold, and any other substance, material or waste that is listed, defined, designated, classified or regulated as hazardous, toxic, a pollutant or a contaminant under any Environmental Law.

"**Impositions**" means all real property taxes, assessments, water and sewer charges, license fees, excises, levies, and other governmental charges of every kind and nature whatsoever, together with all interest and penalties thereon, that may be levied, assessed or imposed upon the Property or upon the Rents or upon Mortgagee by reason of its interest in the Property or this Mortgage.

"**Indebtedness**" means all principal, interest, fees, costs, expenses and other amounts, whether now existing or hereafter arising, that are or become payable by Mortgagor to Mortgagee under the Note or any other Loan Document, including, without limitation, the unpaid principal balance of the Loan, all accrued and unpaid interest thereon (including interest accruing at the Default Rate and, to the extent permitted by applicable law, interest accruing after the commencement of any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding), the Late Charge, the Yield Maintenance Premium, all advances made by Mortgagee under **Article 11**, and all costs of enforcement, collection, foreclosure and defense.

"**Initial Advance**" means the advance of $12,500,000 of Loan proceeds made by Mortgagee to or for the account of Mortgagor on the Closing Date.

"**Insurance Premiums**" means the premiums for all insurance required to be maintained under **Article 8** and **Section 7.6**.

"**Land**" means the real property described in **Exhibit A**, together with all rights, titles, interests, privileges, easements, hereditaments and appurtenances thereto.

"**Land Use Restriction**" or "**LUR**" means that certain land use restriction and institutional control recorded in Deed Book 1203, Page 89, in the RMC Office, imposed by SCDHEC in connection with SCDHEC Site Identification No. SC-29403-0772 and the No Further Action determination dated August 12, 2021, including each of its terms, conditions and obligations, as more particularly described in **Exhibit E**.

"**Late Charge**" has the meaning given in **Section 15.4**.

"**Leases**" means each and every lease, sublease, subsublease, license, concession agreement, occupancy agreement and other agreement, whether written or oral, now or hereafter existing, under which any Person occupies or is entitled to occupy any portion of the Property or is granted any interest in the Property, together with all guaranties, security agreements, letters of credit and other credit support given in connection therewith, including, without limitation, the leases identified in the Rent Roll attached as **Exhibit D**.

"**Lender**" and "**Mortgagee**" mean Calverley Heritage Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank, insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (EIN 58-2947136), with its principal office at 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, Georgia 31401, and its successors and assigns.

"**Loan**" means the loan in the original principal amount of $14,750,000 made by Mortgagee to Mortgagor under the Note, designated Calverley Heritage Bank Commercial Real Estate Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047.

"**Loan Documents**" means this Mortgage, the Note, the Guaranty Agreement, the Completion Guaranty, the Environmental Indemnity Agreement, the UCC-1 Financing Statement, each agreement, certificate and instrument governing or evidencing any Escrow Fund or reserve (including the Capital Replacement Reserve and the Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve), and each other document, instrument, certificate or agreement now or hereafter executed by Mortgagor, Guarantor or any other Person in favor of or delivered to Mortgagee in connection with the Loan, as each may be amended, restated, supplemented or replaced from time to time.

"**Lockout Period**" means the period commencing on the Closing Date and ending on the day immediately preceding the twenty-fourth (24th) monthly anniversary of the date of the Note.

"**Material Adverse Effect**" means any event, circumstance, change or condition that, individually or in the aggregate with other events, circumstances, changes or conditions, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the value, ownership, use, occupancy or operation of the Property, (b) the financial condition, business, assets or operations of Mortgagor or Guarantor, (c) the ability of Mortgagor or Guarantor to perform its obligations under the Loan Documents, or (d) the validity, enforceability, perfection or priority of the Lien of this Mortgage or of any other Loan Document.

"**Maturity Date**" means April 15, 2030, or such earlier date on which the entire Indebtedness becomes due and payable, whether by acceleration, prepayment or otherwise.

"**Mortgagor**" and "**Borrower**" mean Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company (South Carolina Secretary of State Filing No. 2024-0011287; EIN 84-6213750), with its principal office at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401, and its permitted successors and assigns.

"**Net Operating Income**" means, for any period, the excess, if any, of (a) all gross revenues of Mortgagor derived from the ownership and operation of the Property and actually collected during such period, including base rent, additional rent and expense reimbursements, over (b) all operating expenses of the Property actually paid or accrued during such period in accordance with GAAP, including Impositions, Insurance Premiums, utilities, repairs and maintenance, common area maintenance, management fees not exceeding four percent (4.00%) of gross revenues, legal and accounting fees, and deposits made during such period into the Capital Replacement Reserve. Net Operating Income shall be calculated without deduction for (i) debt service on the Loan, (ii) capital expenditures, (iii) depreciation, amortization or other non-cash charges, (iv) income or franchise taxes, and (v) any expense for which Mortgagor is reimbursed by a Tenant, and shall exclude (A) security deposits, (B) the proceeds of any casualty insurance or Condemnation award, (C) capital contributions and loans to Mortgagor, (D) interest or investment income, and (E) extraordinary or non-recurring items. Gross revenues shall exclude all rent and other amounts payable by any Tenant that is more than sixty (60) days delinquent, and all rent attributable to free-rent, abated, discounted or other concessionary periods.

"**Note**" means the Promissory Note of even date herewith in the original principal amount of $14,750,000 executed by Mortgagor and payable to the order of Mortgagee, as the same may be amended, restated, extended, renewed or replaced from time to time.

"**Permitted Exceptions**" means those matters described in **Exhibit B** and only those matters, together with such other exceptions to title as Mortgagee may approve in writing in its sole discretion and which are identified in the Title Policy as issued at closing.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, joint venture, trust, estate, unincorporated organization, Governmental Authority or other entity.

"**Project**" means the renovation and improvement of the Improvements in accordance with the Approved Renovation Budget and the Plans and Specifications.

"**Property**" means, collectively, the Land, the Improvements and all other property, real, personal and mixed, tangible and intangible, described in **Article 3**, together with all Rents and other Collateral.

"**Related Entities**" means Guarantor, Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, Harborline Capital Advisors LLC, and each Affiliate of any of them.

"**Rent Roll**" means the rent roll and lease abstracts for the Property dated as of March 1, 2025, attached as **Exhibit D**, as the same is updated and certified to Mortgagee from time to time under **Section 7.9**.

"**Rents**" means all rents, issues, profits, revenues, income, royalties, license fees, concession fees, proceeds, issues, and other sums of every kind now or hereafter payable under or in connection with the Leases or the use or occupancy of the Property, together with all security deposits, advance rentals, parking income, percentage rent, expense reimbursements, tax and insurance pass-throughs, and all other charges and recoveries.

"**Renovation Costs**" means all hard and soft costs of the Project, including all amounts payable under the GC Contract, all architectural, engineering, permitting, inspection, construction management and legal costs, all tenant improvement allowances, all leasing commissions, and all contingency amounts, in each case consistent with the Approved Renovation Budget.

"**Renovation Holdback**" means the portion of the Loan proceeds in the amount of $2,250,000 retained by Mortgagee and disbursed on a Draw basis in accordance with **Article 9** and **Article 10**.

"**SCDHEC**" means the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control.

"**SOFR Floor**" means three percent (3.00%) per annum.

"**SPE Covenants**" means the single-purpose entity and separateness covenants set forth in **Section 7.4** and in **Article 6**.

"**Substantial Completion**" means the completion of all work comprising the Project in accordance with the Plans and Specifications, as certified by Mortgagor's architect of record, together with the issuance by the City of Charleston of a certificate of occupancy (or an equivalent certificate of completion) for the renovated portions of the Improvements.

"**Substantial Completion Deadline**" means June 15, 2026, being fourteen (14) months after the anticipated Closing Date, subject to extension only as expressly provided in **Section 10.9**.

"**Survey**" means the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey of the Land prepared by Cartwright Land Surveying LLC, dated January 15, 2025 (and re-certified to a date within ninety (90) days of the Closing Date), conforming to the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys and Table A items required by the Title Insurer.

"**Tenant**" means each Person obligated as lessee, tenant, subtenant, licensee or occupant under any Lease.

"**Term Sheet**" means the executed Term Sheet — Commercial Real Estate Loan dated April 1, 2025 between Mortgagor and Mortgagee, Deal Reference CHB CRE Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047.

"**Title Insurer**" means Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc., through its authorized agent Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC.

"**Title Policy**" means the ALTA Loan Policy of title insurance (06-17-06 form with South Carolina modifications) to be issued by the Title Insurer in the amount of $14,750,000 insuring the Lien of this Mortgage as a first-priority lien on the Land and Improvements, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, together with each endorsement required by Mortgagee, including, without limitation, the zoning, access, survey, comprehensive, future advance, contiguity and (if obtainable) survey/encroachment endorsements required by Section 5.6 of the Term Sheet.

"**Treasury Rate**" has the meaning given in **Section 16.2(b)**.

"**UCC-1 Financing Statement**" means the UCC-1 financing statement naming Mortgagor, as debtor, and Mortgagee, as secured party, to be filed with the South Carolina Secretary of State and recorded as a fixture filing in the RMC Office.

"**Yield Maintenance Period**" means the period commencing on the twenty-fourth (24th) monthly anniversary of the date of the Note and ending on the forty-eighth (48th) monthly anniversary of the date of the Note.

"**Yield Maintenance Premium**" has the meaning given in **Section 16.2**.

# ARTICLE 2 — MORTGAGE, GRANTING CLAUSE AND LEGAL DESCRIPTION

**2.1 Property Mortgaged.** Without limiting the generality of the granting clause set forth immediately preceding Article 1, and in addition to the Land and Improvements, this Mortgage encumbers and covers, and Mortgagor hereby mortgages and grants a security interest in, the following:

**(a)** the fee simple interest in the Land, as more particularly described in **Exhibit A**, together with all Improvements, and all tenements, hereditaments, appurtenances, easements, rights, privileges, reversions, remainders, development rights and all right, title and interest of Mortgagor in and to any streets, ways, alleys, strips or gores of land adjoining the Land, including, without limitation, that certain strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 and conveyed to Mortgagor's predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128, Page 443, in the RMC Office;

**(b)** all buildings, structures, improvements, fixtures, building systems and component parts now or hereafter located on, affixed to or used in connection with the Land, including, without limitation, all HVAC equipment and controls, the passenger elevator and all elevator equipment, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, life-safety and fire-protection systems, roof membrane systems, windows, façade elements (including the decorative iron balcony on the King Street elevation), paving, landscaping and lighting;

**(c)** all personal property, equipment, machinery, furniture, furnishings, trade fixtures, inventory, supplies, tools, materials, appliances and other goods owned by Mortgagor and used in connection with the ownership, operation, renovation, management, leasing or maintenance of the Property, including, without limitation, all equipment and materials delivered to the Property for the Project, whether or not yet installed, and all building materials and construction materials now or hereafter situated on the Land;

**(d)** all accounts, deposit accounts, chattel paper, instruments, letters of credit, letter-of-credit rights, investment property, moneys, cash and cash equivalents, credits, claims, refunds and deposits, including all Escrow Funds, all reserves, impounds, escrows and holdbacks established in connection with the Loan, all tenant security deposits (subject to the rights of Tenants), all utility deposits, and all interest and earnings thereon;

For purposes of such filing: (a) the "debtor" is Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company, whose chief executive office, mailing address and principal place of business are 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401, EIN 84-6213750, and whose organizational identification number issued by the South Carolina Secretary of State is 2024-0011287; (b) the "secured party" is Calverley Heritage Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank, whose mailing address is 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, Georgia 31401, EIN 58-2947136; (c) the fixtures are or are to be located on the real property described in **Exhibit A**, located in the City of Charleston, County of Charleston, State of South Carolina, as more particularly described in this Mortgage; and (d) this Mortgage is recorded in the real estate records of Charleston County, South Carolina.

**3.3 Types of Collateral.** The Collateral includes, without limitation, all of the following, whether now existing or hereafter arising: accounts; as-extracted collateral (to the extent applicable); chattel paper; commercial tort claims described on a schedule delivered by Mortgagor and accepted by Mortgagee; deposit accounts; documents; equipment; fixtures; general intangibles; goods; instruments; inventory; investment property; letter-of-credit rights; money; and all supporting obligations, proceeds, products, accessions and substitutions of or relating to any of the foregoing.

**3.4 Purchase-Money and After-Acquired Collateral; No Consent to Encumbrance.** Mortgagor shall not create, incur, assume or permit to exist any security interest in, or lien on, any Collateral other than to Mortgagee. If Mortgagor acquires any goods constituting part of the Collateral that are subject to a purchase-money security interest not approved in writing by Mortgagee, the acquisition shall constitute an Event of Default. Mortgagee's security interest attaches automatically to all after-acquired Collateral and to all proceeds without further action by Mortgagor.

**3.5 Financing Statements and Perfection.** Mortgagor authorizes Mortgagee to file, at Mortgagor's expense, the UCC-1 Financing Statement with the South Carolina Secretary of State, a fixture filing in the RMC Office, and any continuation statements, amendments, protective filings, notices of federal tax lien filings, and such other filings as Mortgagee deems necessary or desirable, including filings in any jurisdiction in which Mortgagor changes its residence, place of organization or location, name or identity or structure. Mortgagor shall (a) maintain its organization under the laws of the State of South Carolina and its principal place of business and chief executive office at the address set forth in Section 3.2, (b) not change its name, identity, type of organization, jurisdiction of organization, organizational identification number or place of business without notifying Mortgagee at least thirty (30) days in advance in writing, and (c) cooperate fully with Mortgagee in all filings and searches necessary to maintain perfection of Mortgagee's security interest with first priority in the Collateral.

**3.6 Lender's Right to Possession and Control.** Mortgagor shall promptly upon Mortgagee's demand execute and deliver such account control agreements, custodial arrangements, consents, waivers and other documentation as Mortgagee may reasonably require to perfect and protect its security interest in deposit accounts, investment property, letter-of-credit rights and chattel paper. Mortgagor shall deposit all Rents and other income from the Property into an account of Mortgagor maintained in accordance with **Section 7.12** and shall, upon Mortgagee's demand following an Event of Default, deposit all such funds into a controlled account, lockbox or cash collateral account under Mortgagee's sole control; if Mortgagor fails to do so within three (3) Business Days after demand, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default.

# ARTICLE 4 — FUTURE ADVANCES AND PRIORITY

**4.1 Future Advances.** This Mortgage is given to secure not only the Initial Advance but also all future advances and disbursements made by Mortgagee under the Loan Documents, including, without limitation, the Renovation Holdback and all Disbursements made under **Article 10**, and all protective advances made under **Article 11**. All such obligations and advances, whether obligatory or optional, and whether or not made pursuant to a commitment in existence on the date of recording of this Mortgage, together with all interest thereon, shall be secured by this Mortgage and shall have priority as of the date and time of recording of this Mortgage to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

**4.2 Renovation Holdback as Obligatory Advance.** Mortgagor and Mortgagee acknowledge that the Renovation Holdback constitutes an obligatory advance under a commitment existing at the time this Mortgage is recorded, and that this Mortgage secures the Renovation Holdback with the same priority as the Initial Advance. Mortgagee shall obtain, at Mortgagor's expense, the future advance endorsement of the Title Policy described in Section 5.6 of the Term Sheet. Mortgagor shall not take any position, in any proceeding, inconsistent with the priority of Mortgagee's Lien securing the Renovation Holdback.

**4.3 Cross-Default and Cross-Security.** A default or event of default under any other Loan Document shall constitute an Event of Default under this Mortgage, and an Event of Default under this Mortgage shall constitute a default under each other Loan Document. Any amounts paid or applied by Mortgagee under any Loan Document shall be deemed applied under all Loan Documents as Mortgagee may elect.

**4.4 No Waiver of Priority.** No increase in the amount secured, no advance made after the occurrence of an Event of Default, no forbearance, and no other act or omission of Mortgagee shall impair, waive, subordinate or otherwise affect the priority of this Mortgage.

# ARTICLE 5 — ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT OF LEASES, RENTS, ISSUES AND PROFITS

**5.1 Absolute Present Assignment.** Mortgagor hereby unconditionally, absolutely and presently grants, bargains, sells, conveys, transfers, assigns and sets over to Mortgagee, without reservation and without any limitation other than as expressly set forth in this Article 5, all of Mortgagor's right, title and interest in, to and under (a) each and every Lease now existing or hereafter arising affecting the Property, including, without limitation, each Lease identified in the Rent Roll, together with all extensions, renewals, amendments, restatements, replacements and guaranties thereof, and (b) all Rents, issues, profits, income, revenues and other sums now or hereafter due, payable or accruing under or with respect to any Lease or the use, occupancy or enjoyment of the Property. This assignment is an absolute and present assignment and not a collateral assignment or an assignment as additional security, and it is effective immediately upon execution of this Mortgage, without regard to any act, event, condition or default, and without the necessity of any further instrument or action by Mortgagor. This assignment is intended to constitute an absolute assignment of rents within the meaning of the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act, Chapter 3, Title 29 of the South Carolina Code of Laws, as amended (the "**Assignment of Rents Act**").

**5.2 Perfection; Authority to Assign.** Mortgagor acknowledges that, under the Assignment of Rents Act, this assignment of Rents is perfected upon recording of this Mortgage in the RMC Office, and that Mortgagee's right to enforce the assignment, including its right to collect the Rents, arises upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default and upon written notice to the applicable Tenants. Mortgagor represents, warrants and covenants that (a) it is the owner of and has the full right, power and authority to absolutely and presently assign each Lease and all Rents; (b) it has not previously assigned, pledged, hypothecated or otherwise encumbered any Lease or any Rents, and has granted no Person any right to collect any Rents other than the revocable license granted in **Section 5.3**; (c) each Lease is in full force and effect, and neither Mortgagor nor, to Mortgagor's knowledge, any Tenant is in default thereunder; (d) no Rents have been prepaid more than one (1) month in advance other than as disclosed in the Rent Roll; and (e) specifically and without limitation of the foregoing, Mortgagor has the full right and authority to absolutely assign all Rents under that certain lease with Lowcountry Provisions Inc. (Bay 1, 520 King Street), notwithstanding that such Lease contains no assignment or subletting provision.

**5.3 Revocable License to Mortgagor.** So long as no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, Mortgagor shall have a revocable, non-assignable license to collect, use and enjoy the Rents in the ordinary course of the operation of the Property, subject to the terms of the Loan Documents. The license granted in this Section 5.3 is granted solely for the purpose of permitting Mortgagor to operate the Property and is not a retransfer or reassignment of the Rents. The license shall be deemed revoked automatically, without further notice, upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, and Mortgagee may, in addition, revoke the license by written notice to Mortgagor.

**5.4 Enforcement Upon Default.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, and upon written notice from Mortgagee to the Tenants (or any of them), Mortgagee shall be entitled, without the necessity of obtaining a court order, appointing a receiver or taking any other action, to (a) collect all Rents directly from the Tenants, (b) enforce the Leases and institute and prosecute all proceedings in the name of Mortgagor or Mortgagee, as Mortgagee may elect, for the collection of Rents, the enforcement of any Lease, the eviction of any Tenant, the recovery of possession or the protection or preservation of the Property, (c) settle, compromise, release, extend or modify in any respect any claim or right under any Lease, in Mortgagee's sole discretion, and (d) do all such other acts and things as Mortgagee may deem necessary or advisable to enforce the assignment made in this Article 5. Mortgagor hereby irrevocably constitutes and appoints Mortgagee as Mortgagor's attorney-in-fact, coupled with an interest, with full power of substitution, for the purposes described in this Section 5.4, which power of attorney may be exercised only upon and during the continuance of an Event of Default. Each Tenant is hereby authorized and directed, upon receipt of written notice from Mortgagee, to pay all Rents directly to Mortgagee or its designee, and Mortgagor hereby irrevocably authorizes and directs each Tenant so to pay, and agrees that any payment made in accordance with such notice shall discharge the Tenant's obligations with respect to such amounts.

**5.5 Tenants Protected; No Liability of Mortgagee.** No Tenant shall be liable to Mortgagor for any Rents paid to Mortgagee in accordance with this Article 5. Mortgagee shall have no obligation to perform any obligation of Mortgagor as landlord under any Lease, to pay or discharge any operating expense, or to maintain or repair the Property, unless and until Mortgagee has actually entered into possession of the Property, and Mortgagor shall remain solely responsible for all landlord obligations under the Leases. The exercise by Mortgagee of any right under this Article 5 shall not constitute an assumption by Mortgagee of any obligation of Mortgagor under any Lease, shall not constitute Mortgagee a mortgagee in possession with respect to obligations to Tenants, and shall not be deemed to constitute an attornment by any Tenant to Mortgagee.

**5.6 Subordination of Leases; Estoppels; SNDAs.** Each Lease now or hereafter existing is and shall be subject and subordinate to this Mortgage and to all renewals, extensions, modifications and consolidations hereof, and Mortgagee may, at its election, require that any Lease be so subordinated in form reasonably acceptable to Mortgagee, *provided* that Mortgagee shall, upon the request of Mortgagor, enter into a commercially reasonable subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreement ("**SNDA**") with any Tenant that is not in default under its Lease, in form reasonably acceptable to Mortgagee. Mortgagor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, and shall deliver to Mortgagee within the applicable time period, (a) an estoppel certificate from each Tenant in accordance with Section 12.1 of the Term Sheet, and (b) an executed SNDA from each Tenant in accordance with Section 12.1 of the Term Sheet. Mortgagor acknowledges that the leases identified on the Rent Roll with Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC and Tidemark Consulting Group LLC each contain a subordination and estoppel provision, and that the lease with Lowcountry Provisions Inc. contains neither an assignment or subletting provision nor an estoppel certificate or SNDA obligation. Accordingly, Mortgagor shall (i) cause Lowcountry Provisions Inc. to deliver an estoppel certificate and an SNDA as a condition to closing, and (ii) thereafter use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, at the next renewal, extension or amendment of the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease (and in any event no later than the tenant's exercise of its renewal option, for which notice is due on or before March 31, 2027), a lease amendment adding customary assignment and subletting provisions, a consent to this assignment of Rents, an estoppel certificate obligation and an SNDA obligation, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Mortgagee, and shall deliver a copy of each such amendment to Mortgagee within five (5) Business Days after execution.

**5.7 Security Deposits.** Mortgagor shall hold all security deposits and advance rentals in trust for the Tenants under the applicable Leases and shall not apply any security deposit except in accordance with the applicable Lease and applicable law. Mortgagor acknowledges that security deposits remain the property of the Tenants and are not the property of Mortgagee; the Lien and assignment granted under this Mortgage extend to Mortgagor's interest in such deposits, subject in all respects to the rights of the Tenants. Upon Mortgagee's request following an Event of Default, Mortgagor shall deliver to Mortgagee an accounting of all security deposits held, together with all documentation necessary to transfer such deposits (or the obligation to return them) to Mortgagee or to a successor owner of the Property.

**5.8 New Leases.** All Leases hereafter executed by Mortgagor shall be subject in all respects to this Mortgage and to the Assignment of Rents Act and shall, unless Mortgagee otherwise consents in writing, contain a provision (a) subordinating the Lease to this Mortgage and to any renewals, extensions and modifications thereof, (b) requiring the Tenant to attorn to any purchaser at foreclosure or to any successor owner of the Property, (c) requiring the Tenant to deliver estoppel certificates within ten (10) Business Days of request, and (d) requiring the Tenant to pay all Rents to Mortgagee upon notice following an Event of Default. Mortgagor shall deliver a fully executed copy of each Lease, and of each amendment, renewal, extension, termination or surrender thereof, to Mortgagee within ten (10) Business Days after execution or receipt, as required by Section 7.3(e) of the Term Sheet and **Section 7.9**.

**5.9 No Merger; Continuing Assignment.** This Article 5 shall not merge with or into any decree of foreclosure, any deed given in lieu of foreclosure, or any other instrument, and shall remain in full force and effect until the Indebtedness has been paid in full and this Mortgage has been released of record. No collection of Rents by Mortgagee, and no application of Rents to the Indebtedness, shall cure any Event of Default, satisfy any provision of this Mortgage, or affect the Lien of this Mortgage on the Property.
